answer: Proof-of-personhood quorums resist sybil attacks: periodically, randomly grouped agents mutually attest that each member is distinct and human-backed, and a group certifying a duplicate gets slashed. The attacker must corrupt an unpredictable cross-section of honest agents, since quorums form only after its fake identities commit, and the cost spirals with every fake. Fee nectar flows to quorums that survive later audits, rewarding vigilance over volume. Each passed audit becomes a pearl of portable proof carried forward, so newcomers without one face rate limits and fresh floods gain little.
